name: Ahira
overview: Ahira was a male leader from the tribe of Naphtali during the time of the Exodus. He served as the head of the tribe of Naphtali at the time of the census recorded in Numbers 1:15. His leadership role was significant during this foundational period for the nation of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahira means either '[my] brother is my friend' or 'my brother is evil,' reflecting possible Hebrew interpretations. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God, but it carries meaningful connotations within the biblical context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Ahira was the father of Enan, establishing a direct family connection. Beyond this, no additional familial relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ahira's importance lies in his role as the appointed leader of the tribe of Naphtali during the census in the wilderness. This census was a critical step in organizing the Israelite community for their journey and military readiness. His leadership contributed to the orderly structure God established among His people during the Exodus.
